slides.title: Temporal Tactile Encoding and Compliance for Intent-Aware Robot-to-Human Bimanual Handover
slides.highlight: This work uses a VLA model with temporal tactile encoding and compliance control to better infer human taking intent during handovers. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and understanding the state of hybrid human-AI team interactions.

card.one_liner: A multimodal humanoid handover system combining temporal tactile encoding and compliance for reliable, intent-aware object release.
card.key_idea: Finetunes a VLA model (GR00T 1.5) using RGB, proprioception, and a frozen autoencoder that compresses ~0.9s of tactile history, paired with a low-level compliance controller.
card.evaluation: Human-subject study (10 participants) comparing full system vs. no-tactile and no-compliance baselines using success rates, release delay, and subjective questionnaires.
card.limitation: Occasional failures occur during impulsive pulls that mimic genuine taking intent, and generalization to unseen objects or grasps remains unexplored.

slides.title: DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination
slides.highlight: DeCAL introduces adaptive visuo-tactile fusion and latent co-imagination to handle contact-rich interactions, contributing to the multimodal perception of physical states relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: DeCAL is a physically-grounded VLA model enhancing contact-rich dexterous manipulation through adaptive visuo-tactile fusion and co-imagination.
card.key_idea: A Mixture-of-Transformers architecture using a contact-aware gating mechanism for tactile integration and a latent co-imagination module to jointly predict future visual and tactile dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six real-world dexterous tasks against baselines like GR00T N1.6 and InternVLA-A1, achieving a 71% average success rate and strong OOD generalization.
card.limitation: Dependence on accurate tactile perception (susceptible to noise/drift) and lack of fingertip force feedback during human teleoperation demonstrations.

slides.title: CR-VLA-Force: Learning Control-aware Compliance VLA Model for Robust Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
slides.tldr: CONTROL-AWARE COMPLIANCE VLA FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: The proposed CC-VLA framework utilizes a multimodal mixture-of-experts to integrate force signal sequences and vision-language features, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception for hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: CC-VLA improves contact-rich robotic manipulation by integrating a force-aware VLA model with an adaptive compliance controller.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical framework using a multimodal MoE, historical force sequence encoder, and multi-stage training to predict action chunks and feedforward forces for a VLA-guided adaptive compliance controller.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four real-world tasks (button-pressing, plug-insertion, window-opening, board-wiping) against baselines like Diffusion Policy and ForceVLA; showed superior success rates and force-tracking precision.
card.limitation: Relies heavily on precise force control and temporal consistency during teleoperation data acquisition; focuses only on object-level variable impedance.

slides.title: Scene Graph-Driven Haptic Feedback for Safety Enhancement in Robotic Ophthalmic Surgery via Physically Simulated iOCT
slides.tldr: SCENE GRAPH-DRIVEN HAPTIC FEEDBACK FOR ROBOTIC SURGERY
slides.highlight: This research introduces a haptic feedback system using Scene Graphs and simulated iOCT to reduce needle alignment errors in robotic ophthalmic surgery. The approach enables a safer 'Align-then-Approach' strategy through real-time, context-aware tactile reinforcement.

card.one_liner: A haptic feedback system using Scene Graphs to improve precision in robotic subretinal injections.
card.key_idea: Real-time Scene Graphs translate simulated iOCT visual data into semantic states, which a rule-based engine maps to context-aware vibrotactile cues for the surgeon.
card.evaluation: User study (N=16) using an anthropomorphic phantom; showed 14% reduced alignment error and 8% higher SUS scores with comparable completion times.
card.limitation: Small sample size, lack of tissue deformation, and reliance on simulated rather than clinical iOCT data.

slides.title: Dex-X: Learning Visual-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation From Human Videos with Simulated Interaction
slides.tldr: LEARNING TACTILE MANIPULATION FROM HUMAN VIDEOS VIA SIMULATION
slides.highlight: DEX-X uses simulation as a tactile completion engine to reconstruct hand-object interactions from monocular human videos, enabling the training of visual-tactile policies without robot-side data collection.

card.one_liner: Dex-X learns visual-tactile dexterous manipulation from human videos by using simulation as a tactile completion engine.
card.key_idea: Reconstructs human hand-object interactions in simulation to generate tactile supervision, trains a privileged state-based expert via RL, and distills it into a point-cloud-based visual-tactile policy.
card.evaluation: Tested on a 29-DoF platform across six task categories; achieved 93% success on real-world cube picking and 53% on table-cleaning.
card.limitation: Sensitive to perception errors and large geometry shifts; tactile representation is limited to per-fingertip force magnitudes.

slides.title: BIFTA: Brain-Inspired Few-Shot Tactile Adaptation for Unknown Sensors
slides.highlight: BIFTA enables robotic models to adapt to unknown tactile sensors using small labeled datasets, supporting the development of embodied interaction across heterogeneous hardware for RwB.

card.one_liner: BIFTA enables frozen tactile foundation models to rapidly adapt to unknown sensors using few labeled examples.
card.key_idea: Combines dual-view statistical memory for probability anchors, support-conditioned spectral graphs to repair sensor-shifted geometry, and uncertainty-gated recurrent propagation to integrate reliable neighborhood evidence.
card.evaluation: Tested on SITR, TacVerse Shape, and TacQuad datasets using TVL and Sparsh backbones; significantly outperformed baselines in classification and identity ranking.

slides.title: WM-Craftnet: World Synesthesia Model for Generalizable and Robust Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a world-model-conditioned framework for robust in-hand manipulation using multimodal latent dynamics, contributing to the agent-based modeling of physical interactions relevant to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: WM-Craftnet uses a world-model-conditioned framework to achieve robust, generalizable dexterous in-hand object rotation.
card.key_idea: A Dreamer-style recurrent state-space model learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from noisy depth, tactile, and proprioceptive data, providing a denoised recurrent feature as policy context.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and real-robot tests on multiple objects (z, x, y axes). Outperformed baselines in success rate, rotation rate, and sim-to-real transfer.
card.limitation: Current tasks are short-horizon, and recovery from severe perturbations remains limited when objects leave the hand workspace.

slides.title: TacPAC: Tactile Prediction and Real-Time Action Correction in World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: TacPAC improves contact-rich manipulation by using predicted tactile observations to correct actions in real-time, significantly outperforming vision-only base models.

card.one_liner: TacPAC improves contact-rich manipulation by correcting planned action chunks using real-time tactile feedback against predicted contact.
card.key_idea: A tactile expert corrects action chunks by comparing live tactile images to a cached representation of the predicted contact and plan from a world-action model.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real-robot tasks; achieved 64% average success rate, outperforming T-Rex (48%) and vision-only baselines (22%).
